noticias.titulo: European Commission confirms cyberattack on staff systems using an AI tool; it is not yet known whether data was stolen
noticias.estado: Attack confirmed by the Commission · theft of personal data unconfirmed · attacker unknown
texto: The European Commission has been hit by a cyberattack that knocked out, for several days, the systems staff use to check their pay, request leave and log their hours. The Commission confirmed it on Thursday 19 November, after the story was reported by Politico. According to spokesperson Thomas Regnier, the attackers used ARTEX, a publicly available artificial intelligence (AI) tool designed to look for weaknesses in computer systems.

What was affected? Mainly Sysper, the human resources platform, and the system for reimbursing medical expenses under the staff health insurance scheme. Several applications were switched off as a precaution and most are working again; salaries were paid as normal. According to Euronews, Regnier said the attack was detected on 22 October; Politico, quoted by Tek, reports disruption lasting more than ten days. CERT-EU, the cybersecurity team of the EU institutions, and the European Data Protection Supervisor have been informed.

What we know — and what we don't. An EU official told Politico that the Commission believes it has stopped most of the attack, but does not yet know how far the damage goes. These systems hold staff names, home addresses, contact details and pay grades. Speaking to Euronews, Regnier said there was no evidence of a data breach affecting staff «as a whole» and that there had been no ransom demand; he would not say who was behind it or whether the attack is still going on.

It is not the first case this year: in January the system that manages the Commission's mobile phones was attacked and, in March, about 92 GB of data was stolen from the cloud service hosting the Europa.eu websites. As for ARTEX, it is an open-source program that uses AI agents to test the security of systems; according to Tek, the FBI warned on 13 November that several groups have been using it in attacks since August.

verificacao.nota: Confirmation of the attack, affected systems (Sysper, health insurance/reimbursements), use of the ARTEX tool according to spokesperson Thomas Regnier and the earlier incidents in January and March confirmed by Euronews (19 Nov) and Tek (19 Nov), which quotes Politico; The Next Web (19 Nov) confirms Politico's report. The detection date (22 Oct), the absence of a ransom demand and the remark about staff «as a whole» come from Euronews. The «more than ten days» duration and the EU official's remark come from Politico (quoted). The FBI warning about ARTEX comes from Tek. We did not consult Politico or an official Commission statement directly. It is not known whether data was stolen or who carried out the attack.

noticias.titulo: Hackers publish customer data linked to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan after attacking the companies' suppliers
noticias.estado: Incidents confirmed by all three companies · card numbers and payments unaffected, they say
texto: A cyber-extortion group called n0n has published customer data linked to Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase, the largest bank in the US. On Thursday 19 November, the three companies confirmed incidents at outside suppliers, but insist that their own networks were not attacked, that payments are still working and that card numbers were not exposed.

What was leaked? Mostly marketing data. JPMorgan says the attackers reached information held by suppliers, which may include customer names and email addresses; it will contact those affected and offer free credit monitoring. According to an analysis by Reuters, quoted by Business Standard, the bank's files contain more than 16,000 customer email addresses and about 124 belonging to employees, some with phone numbers and postcodes. According to Newsweek, they appear to belong to customers of Reserve, an invitation-only card for very wealthy clients.

Visa links the case to a supplier in the Asia-Pacific region — the published data mainly concerns customers in Hong Kong, Japan, Australia and other countries in the region. Mastercard speaks of «a limited amount» of email addresses of members of a benefits programme. The group had claimed the attacks on 16 November; the companies have not said which suppliers were attacked, or how.

Why does it matter? Even without card numbers, names and email addresses linked to a bank or a benefits programme make fake messages that try to steal passwords or codes (phishing) more convincing. The advice repeated by experts: be wary of unexpected notices and always check through the bank's app or the number on the back of the card, never through links in the message.

verificacao.nota: Statements by the three companies (incidents at suppliers, no impact on payments or card numbers), the claim by the n0n group on 16 Nov and the figures from Reuters' analysis (more than 16,000 JPMorgan customer email addresses, about 124 employee ones) confirmed by Business Standard (20 Nov, based on Reuters) and Cyber Security News (20 Nov). The link to the Reserve card comes from Newsweek (and from American Banker, quoted by Cyber Security News). We did not consult Reuters directly. The figures are journalists' counts of the published files, not confirmed totals of affected customers; Visa and Mastercard gave no figures.

noticias.titulo: Germany raises its cybersecurity alert to «tense to critical»: with AI, attacks are faster and cheaper
noticias.estado: Official assessment in the BSI's annual report (19 Nov) · does not refer to a specific attack
texto: Germany now considers the cyber threat to be «tense to critical», one step above last year's «tense». The assessment comes from the BSI, Germany's federal IT security agency, in its annual report presented in Berlin on Thursday 19 November with the interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt. The main reason: artificial intelligence (AI) is making attacks «ever faster, cheaper and more targeted».

The figures help explain it. The time between a flaw being made public and the first known attack exploiting it fell from 53 days to 25 and, in the second quarter of 2026, to eight; Dobrindt said there are already cases of just a few hours. The BSI reports around 75,400 infected devices a day in Germany to internet providers, 89% more than before — 88% are Android, and some cheap uncertified devices come with malicious software already installed at the factory.

The BSI's president, Claudia Plattner, called for an end to «complacency» and said AI has already found flaws that went unnoticed for around 20 years. She named Russia, China, Iran and North Korea as the origin of many attacks, although it is not always clear whether the states direct them or merely tolerate them. Small and medium-sized businesses are the most vulnerable target, because there are so many of them and they are often less well protected.

There are positive signs too: according to Reuters, the report acknowledges progress in IT security regulation and says operators of critical infrastructure, subject to stricter rules, are generally better protected — though still with «room for improvement». The report also recalls the attacks in October and November on refrigeration systems in supermarkets in Germany and other European countries.

verificacao.nota: New «tense to critical» level, date and presentation, the role of AI and the line about attacks being «faster, cheaper and more targeted» confirmed by Reuters (republished by Insurance Journal, 19 Nov) and t-online (19 Nov). Exploitation times (53, 25 and 8 days), infected devices, statements by Plattner and Dobrindt and the countries named come from t-online; progress on regulation and the line about critical infrastructure come from Reuters. Reuters gives figures for a BSI index (124 to 238 points) and t-online reports a 50% rise in a new index; as we could not reconcile the two, we did not use them. We did not consult the BSI report or the Interior Ministry's press release directly (it would not open).

noticias.titulo: Anthropic opens more than 30% up on its stock market debut, but ends the first day with a 17% gain
noticias.estado: Result of the first day of trading (19 Nov) · company still loss-making · US markets closed lower
texto: The debut went well, but with ups and downs. Shares in Anthropic, the company that makes the artificial intelligence (AI) assistant Claude, began trading on Thursday 19 November on the Nasdaq in New York. The first trade was at $111.50, more than 30% above the $83 offer price. At the close they were worth $97.17: a gain of about 17% on the first day, according to the AP news agency.

During the session, the shares reached almost $115 and fell to close to $93, according to market data cited by the StockTitan website. At the open, the company was briefly worth about $2 trillion, compared with $1.5 trillion at the offer price. Demand was strong: according to remarks cited by AP, there were about six times more orders for shares than shares on sale.

The enthusiasm did not spread to the rest of the market. The main US indices closed down close to 2%, and shares in AI-linked companies such as Nvidia and AMD gave up their morning gains. Why does this matter? Anthropic raised about $81 billion, the largest stock market listing ever, but it is still loss-making and has committed to spending about $900 billion on computing and infrastructure. For analyst Dan Ives, quoted by AP, it is «a big win» for the tech sector after tense weeks around Nvidia.

verificacao.nota: First trade at $111.50, close at $97.17 (+17%), $83 offer price, $1.5 trillion valuation at the offer and ~$2.01 trillion at the open, demand six times higher (remark by Thackray, quoted by AP without our having confirmed his role), $81 billion raised, losses and $900 billion commitments confirmed by AP (republished by BNN Bloomberg, 19 Nov). Opening at 11:48 (New York time), high of $114.99 and low of $92.72 and falls of about 2% in the indices (measured by funds that track them) according to StockTitan, which cites CNBC; the high and low were not confirmed by a second source. Bloomberg and other sites put the amount raised at $107.3 billion (a figure that may include a direct sale to companies), not confirmed. The CNBC, CNN and NBC pages could not be opened. Transparency: this newspaper is produced with AI tools, including Anthropic models.

noticias.titulo: European Central Bank compares AI giants' borrowing to the dotcom and subprime bubbles
noticias.estado: Warning in the ECB's financial stability review (18 Nov) · risk assessment, not a forecast of a crisis
texto: The European Central Bank (ECB) is worried about how the race for artificial intelligence (AI) is being paid for. In the financial stability review published on Wednesday 18 November, it warns that the big US tech companies are increasingly financing data centres with debt. That shift, the bank writes, recalls the bubble in internet companies (the «dotcoms», around 2000) and the one in high-risk mortgage lending (the «subprime» bubble that led to the 2008 crisis).

The numbers help explain why. According to the ECB, companies such as Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, Oracle and Anthropic had, by mid-2026, more than $4 trillion in commitments that do not show up as debt in their accounts: long-term contracts with those who build data centres and buy chips. The bank also points to «circular financing» (chipmakers financing their own customers), which makes real demand hard to measure, and to the short life of AI chips: one to three years, while the debt that pays for them lasts much longer.

And Europe? The ECB says euro area banks are not significantly exposed, but that European investment funds and households hold more and more shares and debt in these companies and could suffer losses. If the cycle goes wrong in the US, it warns, the euro area economy would shrink too. The bank notes that, so far, tech companies' profits have kept up with expectations, and that the dotcom bubble caused only a mild recession because it was paid for mainly with shares rather than debt.

verificacao.nota: Date, sentence on «historical parallels» with the dotcom and subprime bubbles, off-balance-sheet commitments above $4 trillion (second quarter of 2026), circular financing, one-to-three-year useful life of AI equipment and risks to the euro area confirmed in the ECB's own review (box on the debt financing of AI) and by Fortune (18 Nov). List of companies analysed and remark by ECB vice-president Boris Vujčić on banks' limited exposure according to Fortune. The review does not forecast a crisis; it describes risks.

noticias.titulo: Microsoft reportedly close to selling access to OpenAI models to TikTok owner ByteDance; US Congress demands explanations
noticias.estado: Talks reported by The Information (18 Nov) · no deal confirmed · congressional committee asks Microsoft for a briefing
texto: Microsoft is reportedly in advanced talks to sell more AI services to ByteDance, the Chinese company that owns TikTok: about $500 million extra on its Azure cloud, mainly to use OpenAI's models. The news was reported on Wednesday 18 November by the website The Information, cited by other outlets. On the same day, the US House of Representatives committee on China asked Microsoft for a meeting to explain the deal.

Why is this controversial? OpenAI bars most Chinese companies from using its models, but Microsoft, which has the right to sell them through Azure, does not apply the same restrictions. According to The Information, OpenAI was unhappy about the talks and had already complained about Chinese companies copying its work by training rival models on its AI's answers. The report does not say ByteDance has done so.

«Microsoft should not sell AI tools to ByteDance,» said the committee's chairman, Republican John Moolenaar, who accuses US tech companies of «playing both sides» of the AI race between the US and China. Neither Microsoft nor ByteDance commented publicly in the sources consulted. The case comes in the week the US began requiring a licence for advanced chips in data centres in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia, to stop remote access by Chinese companies.

verificacao.nota: Talks worth about $500 million on Azure, mainly for OpenAI models, and OpenAI's displeasure according to The Information (cited by TNW, which says it has not confirmed the report; the original article is paywalled and was not opened). Request for a bipartisan briefing from Microsoft and Moolenaar's remarks confirmed in the committee's official press release and by Reuters (via Yahoo), both dated 18 Nov. No confirmed deal and no public reaction from Microsoft, ByteDance or OpenAI in the sources consulted. No deadline for the meeting given.

noticias.titulo: GTA VI arrives on consoles with record numbers — and with PlayStation network failures at launch
noticias.estado: Released on 19 Nov · sales are analysts' estimates · Sony has not explained the failures
texto: Thirteen years after GTA V, Rockstar released Grand Theft Auto VI on Thursday 19 November, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S; no computer version has been announced. It is one of the most anticipated launches ever in video games: according to estimates by the analytics company Sensor Tower, quoted by Tek, more than 17 million copies were sold in pre-orders, worth about $1.65 billion.

The records did not stop there. According to Streams Charts, quoted by Tek, about 7.9 million people watched live streams of the launch at the same time, a high for a video game. Critics applauded too: according to Latin Times, its average score on Metacritic is 99 out of 100, equal to the record of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, from 1998. The game is set in Leonida, a fictional state inspired by Florida, with two protagonists, Jason and Lucia.

Not everything went smoothly. The PlayStation's online network (PSN) had sign-in failures on the eve of the launch and on launch day; Sony acknowledged the problems on the service's status page, but did not explain the cause or link them to the game. There are reports of bugs, such as freezes and crashes early in the story, and the download can reach 212 GB. According to Tek, internet providers in the UK, Australia and New Zealand recorded record traffic peaks.

verificacao.nota: Release date, platforms, Sensor Tower's estimate (about 17 million copies) and PSN failures acknowledged by Sony without explaining the cause confirmed by Tek (19 Nov), Latin Times and IBTimes UK. The $1.65 billion figure, the streaming audience (Streams Charts) and the traffic peaks come from Tek; the Metacritic score of 99 and the bug reports come from Latin Times. The sales figures are third-party estimates, not official Take-Two/Rockstar data. We did not consult Sony or Rockstar directly.

noticias.titulo: British tribunal forces the government to admit it demanded access to Apple's encrypted data
noticias.estado: Tribunal ruling (19 Nov) · the order's legality will only be tried in 2027
texto: The British government can no longer refuse to talk about it. The Investigatory Powers Tribunal, the court that oversees surveillance and the intelligence services in the UK, ruled on Thursday 19 November that the Home Office cannot keep to its position of «neither confirm nor deny» that it sent Apple a secret order to provide access to customers' encrypted data.

Why does it matter? These orders, known as «technical capability notices», can force a company to create a way for the authorities to reach protected data. Apple refuses to open such a «back door» in its encryption and, because of this dispute, stopped offering Advanced Data Protection in the UK, the option that encrypts copies stored in iCloud end to end.

According to City A.M., the tribunal found the government's national security assessment flawed, because the order's existence was already widely known — and had even been confirmed to newspapers through leaks the tribunal describes as «authorised». The technical details of the order remain secret.

What next? Apple's complaint, and a parallel one by the privacy campaign groups Privacy International and Liberty, goes to a full hearing in the first half of 2027, largely open to the public. In other words: the case gains transparency, but the main question — whether the order is lawful — is still to be decided.

verificacao.nota: Date and substance of the ruling (rejection of the «neither confirm nor deny» position) confirmed by City A.M. (19 Nov) and by the page of Blackstone Chambers, a barristers' chambers involved in the case, which identifies the ruling as [2026] UKIPTrib 9. The criticism of the national security assessment, the «authorised» leaks, the withdrawal of Advanced Data Protection and the hearing expected in the first half of 2027 come from City A.M. We did not read the full judgment. Apple and the Home Office had not commented, according to City A.M.

noticias.titulo: Shenzhen: Xi, Trump and Putin close their summit with a «peace declaration» that says nothing about Ukraine or Iran
noticias.estado: Fact: summit ended on 19 Nov with a joint declaration · no concrete agreements on the wars · no new meetings announced
texto: The first three-way summit between the leaders of the US, China and Russia ended on Thursday 19 November in Shenzhen, in southern China, with a «trilateral peace declaration». Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for about an hour and a half. The text covers UN reform, more oil production and dialogue on nuclear risks — but does not mention the war in Ukraine or the one in Iran, according to Euronews and AP.

What does the declaration say? Besides those three points, the three countries defend the immunity of state officials and criticise the International Criminal Court and other courts which, they say, «abuse their jurisdiction», according to AP and Euronews. The text was released by Chinese state media and by Russian officials. There were no joint statements to journalists at the end: the three posed for the family photo without shaking hands, and Trump went straight to the airport.

The tone was upbeat. Trump said the three are «making history» and are uniquely placed to talk about nuclear weapons. Xi spoke of a «positive, constructive and fruitful» summit and argued that nuclear weapons should be banned and destroyed. Putin called it an «important chapter» in diplomacy and said the outcome exceeded expectations. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov admitted that Ukraine was not «the central topic».

In Europe, the reaction was one of suspicion. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the three leaders «disagree on everything» and so «cannot agree on anything», according to Euronews. There are fears that the great powers will decide on Ukraine without Kyiv or the Europeans. Hours after the summit ended, Russia launched a massive missile and drone attack on Ukraine (see next story).

verificacao.nota: Length (about 1h20 according to Euronews; about 90 minutes according to the Washington Post, via Newser), points of the declaration, and quotes from Xi, Putin, Trump, Peskov and Barrot according to Euronews (19 Nov); points of the declaration confirmed by the BBC and AP, and criticism of the International Criminal Court according to AP, both quoted by Newser. noticias.titulo: Russia attacks Ukraine overnight: three Kyiv bridges damaged and at least five dead
noticias.estado: Attack confirmed by Ukrainian authorities · provisional toll · Poland investigating possible entry of objects into its airspace
texto: In the early hours of Friday 20 November, Russia launched an attack lasting several hours on Ukraine with ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones. In Kyiv, three bridges over the Dnipro river were damaged and three people were killed, all employees of the city's water company; about 15 were injured. In Lviv, in the west, the mayor reports two dead. The figures are provisional, according to the Kyiv Independent and the Kyiv Post.

The bridges hit were the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, the Darnytskyi and the Southern Bridge. Traffic between the capital's two banks was severely disrupted, and the mayor, Vitali Klitschko, asked people to avoid driving and businesses to let staff work from home. Several Kyiv districts lost electricity, heating or water. There were also injuries in Kharkiv — including at a hospital hit by a drone — and in the Dnipropetrovsk region, and power cuts in Lviv, Kryvyi Rih and Ivano-Frankivsk.

The attack comes a day after Putin promised a «far more painful» response to the Ukrainian strike that damaged the Crimean Bridge on 17 November, according to the Kyiv Independent. And just hours after the Russian leader left the Shenzhen summit with Trump and Xi. The missiles were fired by Tu-160 strategic bombers that took off from a base in Russia's Far East.

In neighbouring Poland, the armed forces said at around 06:30 local time that «unidentified aerial objects» may have entered the country's airspace, after reports of an explosion near the village of Chmielek, in the east. The military is analysing radar data and has not yet confirmed what happened, according to the Kyiv Post. Rzeszów airport suspended operations and military aircraft were scrambled.

verificacao.nota: Deaths and injuries in Kyiv, damaged bridges, power cuts and Klitschko's appeals according to the Kyiv Independent and the Kyiv Post (20 Nov), confirmed by RBC-Ukraine; deaths in Lviv according to the mayor, Andrii Sadovyi, via the Kyiv Post and RBC-Ukraine. noticias.titulo: UN court finds for the first time that a state committed genocide: Myanmar, against the Rohingya
noticias.estado: Fact: ICJ judgment on 19 Nov, backed by 9 of the 15 judges · final, no appeal · compensation still to be set
texto: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the UN's main court, in The Hague, ruled on Thursday 19 November that Myanmar (formerly Burma) committed genocide against the Muslim Rohingya minority. It is the first time the court has declared that a state committed genocide. The decision was backed by nine of the 15 judges and cannot be appealed, according to Al Jazeera and Observador.

The case was brought to the court by the Gambia in 2019. It concerns the 2017 military offensive in Rakhine State, which killed thousands of Rohingya and forced more than 700,000 to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh. The judges found killings, sexual violence — also used to prevent births within the group — and the systematic destruction of villages to be proven. The court's president, Yuji Iwasawa, said the court was «fully convinced» that acts covered by the Genocide Convention had taken place.

What changes? Myanmar must stop the violence, investigate and try those responsible, allow the safe and voluntary return of refugees, and rebuild or return what was destroyed. Compensation will be decided later, and the country must submit a report to the court within two years. The problem is that the ICJ has no way of enforcing compliance: that would fall to the UN Security Council, where China and Russia can shield Myanmar, Observador notes.

For the Rohingya, it is a long-awaited symbolic victory. About 1.2 million live in refugee camps in Cox's Bazar, in Bangladesh. The Gambia's lead counsel spoke of a «landmark victory». Six judges dissented, arguing that the majority used a less demanding standard of proof than usual. The decision may carry weight in other genocide cases at the ICJ, such as the one South Africa is bringing against Israel.

verificacao.nota: Decision, vote (9–6), final nature, findings, measures ordered and two-year deadline according to Al Jazeera (19 Nov) and the American Society of International Law (ASIL); Iwasawa's quote and the limits on enforcement according to Observador (19 Nov); the Gambia's counsel's quote and refugee figures according to Al Jazeera; dissenting opinions according to ASIL. None of the sources consulted carried an official reaction from Myanmar's regime after the decision; it has always denied the accusations.

noticias.titulo: COP31: fossil fuels disappear from the new draft deal, on the summit's last scheduled day
noticias.estado: Draft of 19 Nov, not the final text · close scheduled for 20 Nov, probably with overtime
texto: The new draft of the deal at the UN climate summit, COP31, in Antalya, Türkiye, no longer talks about moving away from coal, oil and gas. The text was published on the afternoon of Thursday 19 November, the eve of the conference's last scheduled day. Both references to fossil fuels in the first draft, from Monday, were removed, according to Reuters and UN News.

What remains? The text admits that warming will exceed the 1.5°C limit and asks for that overshoot to be as small and short as possible, with «deep, rapid and sustained» emissions cuts. It keeps the call for electricity to reach 35% of the energy used worldwide by 2035 (it is around 23% today), but less firmly. And the figure of $120 billion to help developing countries adapt has been dropped, according to Reuters.

Environmental groups reacted badly. Mohamed Adow, of Power Shift Africa, said the text had «gone backwards» and that, if it stays like this, it will be a «ghost COP». Greenpeace criticised the room given to carbon removal technologies, which, it says, may serve as an excuse to keep producing fossil fuels.

Australian minister Chris Bowen, who leads the negotiations with Türkiye, promised to keep consulting overnight and said he will not leave Antalya without a consensus. The close is scheduled for this Friday, 20 November, but in recent years these summits have ended more than a day after the deadline. Finance, adaptation and the so-called just transition are still unresolved.

verificacao.nota: Content of the new draft, the dropped $120 billion figure, the «35 by 35» goal and the reactions of Power Shift Africa and Greenpeace according to Reuters (via the Express Tribune, 19 Nov); time the draft was published, acknowledgement that 1.5°C will be exceeded, Bowen's quote and outstanding issues according to UN News (19 Nov). At the time of going to press it was not possible to confirm whether a more recent text existed or the exact closing time.

noticias.titulo: Civil service on strike: rubbish uncollected since the night and schools that may not open, four days before the Budget vote
noticias.estado: Strike under way since 00:00 on 20 Nov · first effects according to the unions · turnout not yet known
texto: Schools, health centres, town halls and Tax and Social Security counters may be closed or running at half speed this Friday, 20 November. Public administration workers are on a national strike called by the Frente Comum, which brings together unions linked to the CGTP, the largest trade union confederation. The first effects were felt during the night: according to STAL, the local authority workers' union, rubbish collection stopped in Évora, Loures, Palmela and Seixal, and was "almost totally" halted in Almada, Amadora, Moita, Setúbal and Vila Franca de Xira.

What do the unions want? Rises of at least 15%, with a minimum of €150, a base salary of €1,150 in the civil service from January, and a meal allowance of €13. The deal the Government has planned for 2027 falls well short: a 2.3% rise, at least €60.52, and a meal allowance of €6.30. The Frente Comum's coordinator, Sebastião Santana, says the aim is "to fight against a budget that destroys the public administration", four days before the final vote on the 2027 State Budget.

Doctors (FNAM) and nurses (SEP) have also joined, with minimum services for emergencies, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, dialysis and transplants. Anyone with non-urgent appointments or tests should check whether they are going ahead. Municipal and school buses may fail, but in Lisbon the Metro, Carris and Transtejo are not covered. In the Azores, SATA warned that inter-island flights may be affected.

The week of protests does not end here. On Saturday 21, the CGTP holds a national demonstration in Lisbon. On Tuesday 24, the day of the final Budget vote, there is a rally outside the Assembleia da República, Portugal's parliament. And from 23 to 27, CP train drivers walk out.

noticias.titulo: Budget: PS and Chega pass zero VAT on a basket of food and Montenegro warns "if you want to govern, come to an understanding"
noticias.estado: Fact: zero VAT approved at the detailed stage on 20 Nov (early hours) · voting until 23 Nov · final overall vote on 24 Nov
texto: The second day of voting on the 2027 State Budget ended in the early hours, at 01:34 this Friday, 20 November, with another defeat for the Government. The PS (Socialist) proposal to exempt a basket of essential foods from VAT passed with the votes of Chega, against the PSD, the CDS-PP and the IL; the PCP abstained. The exemption applies from 1 January to 31 March 2027 and can be renewed for another three months after an assessment. The products have not yet been defined: it is up to the Government to choose them.

Who pays? To offset it, the tax break the Government created for landlords charging "moderate" rents of up to €2,300 is scrapped. Those contracts go back to the standard 25% income tax rate. PSD MP Alberto Fonseca says this will push rents up. According to ECO, Chega's parliamentary leader, Pedro Pinto, said the PSD could take this measure to a new vote in the plenary. A PS proposal to cut the fuel tax (ISP) in the first quarter, however, was voted down.

Other measures that passed include a three-year capital gains tax exemption on selling second homes that become a permanent home or go to affordable renting, tax withholding that adjusts to the income of self-employed workers, and an income tax deduction for part of the VAT on cinema tickets. By ECO's count, 105 measures were approved that day, 75 of them from the opposition.

Tempers rose. On Thursday, at a closed-door meeting with PSD and CDS-PP MPs, the prime minister, Luís Montenegro, criticised the opposition's lack of coherence: "If you want to govern, come to an understanding." He also spoke of the risk of an "institutional blockage", according to accounts from those present given to Lusa. The minister of the Presidency, António Leitão Amaro, accused the PS and Chega of forming a "negative and deficit coalition". Voting continues until Monday 23; the final overall vote is on Tuesday 24.

noticias.titulo: Ombudsman's office finds PSP police used batons "widely" against protesters in Rossio; PSP rejects it
noticias.estado: Findings of an Ombudsman's report (19 Nov) · PSP disputes them · IGAI and Public Prosecutor inquiries under way
texto: When the PSP, Portugal's public security police, dismantled the housing protest camp in Rossio, in Lisbon, in the early hours of 1 November, officers used their batons "widely", including on people who were not resisting or were already moving away. That is the conclusion of the National Preventive Mechanism of the Provedoria de Justiça, the Ombudsman's office, which monitored the operation and released its report on Thursday 19 November.

Most of the blows hit lower-risk areas, but there were strikes to the head, chest and spine, areas the PSP's own rules regard as most dangerous. The report also points to dispersal warnings that could barely be heard, difficulties in helping an injured protester in Martim Moniz, and the lack of photographs of the injuries of two detained people. It makes 12 recommendations to the PSP, including tighter rules on baton use and visible identification of each officer.

The PSP does not accept the findings: it says there was no "widespread or indiscriminate" use of the baton, that glass bottles and pyrotechnics were thrown at officers, and that the warnings were given by megaphone. It promises to take the recommendations into account. The Ministry of Internal Administration, headed by Luís Neves, will analyse the report and says any breach of the rules "should have the consequences provided for in law". The General Inspectorate of Internal Administration (IGAI) and the Public Prosecutor's Office already have inquiries open.

noticias.titulo: Lisbon's funiculars: year-old reports point to cable faults in four of them; Moedas denies hiding anything
noticias.estado: Audit reports (Oct–Nov 2025) released on 18 Nov · Moedas denies concealment · final reports expected by March 2027
texto: The cables of four of Lisbon's historic funiculars and lifts — Glória, Lavra, Bica and Santa Justa — did not meet the standards required for this type of equipment. That is what technical audits carried out a year ago say, after the derailment of the Glória funicular, which killed 16 people on 3 September 2025. The reports were only handed to opposition councillors on Wednesday 18 November, following an investigation by TVI/CNN Portugal.

The audits were carried out by CATIM, a technical centre for the metalworking industry, at the request of Carris, the city's transport company, and date from October and November 2025. On Lavra, the conclusion is that it was not safe to operate. Bica needs "significant and urgent" work. At Santa Justa, the cable also fails to meet the standard, but the system has 12 cables and redundant safety mechanisms. Graça, the only one that has reopened (since April), complies overall, with flaws in its evacuation plan.

The opposition accuses the mayor, Carlos Moedas, of lying and hiding the documents; Left Bloc councillor Ricardo Moreira says Moedas is in no position to continue if the findings are confirmed. Moedas denies it: he says he did not know about the reports, which are "technical" and "interim", and that they show he made "the right decision at the right time" by closing the funiculars. What is still unknown? Who is responsible for the accident: the Public Prosecutor's Office and GPIAAF, the body that investigates rail accidents, only expect to conclude by the end of March 2027.

verificacao.nota: Content of the reports confirmed by Lusa (via DN, 18 Nov), TVI/CNN Portugal (18 Nov) and Observador (19 Nov). Moedas's statements according to Observador. The Left Bloc councillor's statement according to TVI; Renascença reports that the Left Bloc in Lisbon is demanding his resignation, but that page was not opened. The sources do not say clearly whether Bica and Santa Justa remain closed; DN says Glória, Lavra, Santa Justa and Bica have been shut since the accident.

noticias.titulo: BepiColombo reaches Mercury: European-Japanese probe fires its engines on Saturday to enter orbit around the planet
noticias.estado: Orbit entry planned for Saturday 21 Nov, according to ESA · exact time not released
texto: After eight years of travel, BepiColombo is at Mercury's doorstep. The mission of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese agency JAXA is due to enter orbit around the planet closest to the Sun on Saturday 21 November, when controllers fire the spacecraft's engines. If all goes to plan, it will be only the second mission ever to orbit Mercury, after NASA's MESSENGER. ESA has not released the time of the manoeuvre.

How do you «park» next to Mercury? With a lot of braking. Close to the Sun, a spacecraft picks up speed and tends to overshoot the planet, so BepiColombo spent years slowing down with flybys of Earth, Venus and Mercury itself. According to ESA, the probe will be gently «caught» by the planet's gravity, in an orbit over the poles. For Tech Times, which cites Space.com, Saturday is not the end but the beginning: it kicks off a series of about 16 manoeuvres over roughly six months. ESA has not confirmed that number.

The next steps have already been set by ESA: on 9 and 10 December the two probes separate — the European MPO, which will map the surface and study the interior, and the Japanese Mio, which will measure the magnetic field and the thin layer of sodium gas around the planet. Science begins in April 2027 and should last about three years, until the fuel runs out. The mission cost €1.6 billion, according to the Guardian. «We're very excited, it's been a long wait», Emma Bunce, of the University of Leicester, who leads one of the instruments, told the paper.

There is a bit of Portugal on board too: according to DN, at the time of the 2018 launch, the company Efacec built and tested electronic equipment for an energetic-particle detector on the European probe, and Portuguese astrophysicist Joana S. Oliveira is part of the science team.

verificacao.nota: Date of 21 Nov, separation on 9–10 Dec and start of science in April 2027 confirmed by ESA (updates page; no November entries as of 19 Nov) and by the Guardian (20 Nov), which adds the cost, the roughly three-year duration and the statements by Emma Bunce and Geraint Jones. The «gentle» capture into a polar orbit comes from ESA's mission design pages, cited by Tech Times (19 Nov); the series of 16 manoeuvres is from Space.com, cited by Tech Times, and has not been confirmed by ESA. None of the sources consulted gives the time of the manoeuvre. The Portuguese involvement comes from a 2018 DN article. noticias.titulo: Engines fail and Japan's Hayabusa2 probe gives up on landing on an asteroid: it will fly past another one in 2028 instead
noticias.estado: New plan announced by JAXA (16–17 Nov) · asteroid flyby planned for April 2028
texto: Japan's Hayabusa2 probe will no longer land on an asteroid in 2031. Japan's space agency, JAXA, announced this week that its ion engines (low-thrust electric engines used for long journeys) are too worn out for the planned trip to the small asteroid 1998 KY26. Instead, the probe will speed past another asteroid, 2015 BM510, in April 2028. The new plan was presented on 16 November to a Japanese government committee and explained to journalists on the 17th.

What went wrong? Hayabusa2 has four ion engines and has been flying for almost 12 years, well beyond what was planned. Three of them wore out earlier than expected and the last one working properly broke down in August, according to the Japanese websites sorae and innovaTopia. The team has kept the probe going by mixing parts from different engines, but does not know how long that will last. Reaching 1998 KY26 would have required more than 10,000 hours of engine time; JAXA concluded it was not realistic.

The new target is small and odd. 2015 BM510 is thought to measure between 17 and 74 metres and spins once every 49 minutes or so. It is a D-type asteroid, considered primitive and possibly rich in organic matter. The probe will pass a few hundred metres away, at about 6 km per second, and should only «see» it some 10 hours beforehand. JAXA admits it will be an extremely difficult flyby.
Hayabusa2 already has quite a track record: in 2020 it brought samples of the asteroid Ryugu back to Earth and, in July this year, it passed about 400 metres from the asteroid Torifune.

cultura.titulo: «The Hunger Games: Amanhecer na Ceifa» (Sunrise on the Reaping): the return to Panem splits critics between «the best in the saga for years» and «more of the same»

ficha.Original title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (2026, United States)
ficha.Director: Francis Lawrence (who also directed four of the saga's five previous films)
ficha.Screenplay: Billy Ray, based on the book by Suzanne Collins
ficha.Cast: Joseph Zada, Mckenna Grace, Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, Kieran Culkin, Glenn Close, Ralph Fiennes
ficha.Release in Portugal: 19 November 2026 (adventure and science fiction; rated M/12; 158 minutes; distributed by Pris Audiovisuais)
ficha.Reviews: Divided reviews: praise from TheWrap, B- from the AV Club, 2.5 out of 5 from the South China Morning Post and a negative review from the Daily Beast

texto: Since yesterday, Thursday 19 November, «The Hunger Games: Amanhecer na Ceifa» (Sunrise on the Reaping), the sixth film in the «Hunger Games» saga, has been showing in Portuguese cinemas. It is a prequel, adapted from Suzanne Collins's book, that goes back 24 years in time to tell the story of the youth of Haymitch Abernathy, Katniss's mentor in the first films. It is directed by Francis Lawrence. At NorteShopping, in Matosinhos, there are screenings from 12:30, at least until Wednesday 25.

Haymitch, played by the Australian Joseph Zada, is a boy from the poor District 12. His birthday falls on the day of the «reaping», the draw that picks the young people forced to fight to the death in a show broadcast across the country. But this is a special edition, the 50th, and each district must send twice as many contestants. The rest is for cinemagoers to find out. Around him are familiar faces in younger versions: Jesse Plemons as Plutarch Heavensbee, Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket and Kieran Culkin as the host Caesar Flickerman, with Ralph Fiennes as President Snow.

The strengths, for those who liked it. William Bibbiani, of TheWrap, thinks it is the best film in the saga since «Catching Fire» (2013): it balances spectacle with a critique of violence turned into entertainment, has a look inspired by 1970s television and a Zada who recalls Woody Harrelson without imitating him. Jesse Hassenger, of the AV Club, praises Lawrence's direction, the visual energy and the fact that the film does not give in to fan service. Even the harshest critic, Nick Schager, of the Daily Beast, singles out Plemons and Culkin's sardonic Caesar.

The weaknesses are also clear. The AV Club gives it a B- and speaks of a «fill-in» chapter, with too many introductions and brief cameos, weak digital effects and 158 minutes that you feel. James Mottram, in the South China Morning Post, gives it 2.5 out of 5 and finds it «by the numbers», with neither tension nor emotion. The Daily Beast is the most severe: uneven pacing, flat characters and battles without suspense. In short, according to the assessment drawn from the reviews consulted: a well-produced film that will please followers of the saga, but does not convince everyone that there was still much left to tell.

cultura.titulo: Alice Neel, the «collector of souls»: she painted neighbours, activists and Andy Warhol — and comes to Portugal for the first time, at Serralves

ficha.Born and died: 28 January 1900, in Merion Square, Pennsylvania (United States); 13 October 1984, in New York
ficha.Essential work: «Carlos Enríquez» (1926), «Pat Whalen» (1935), «Puerto Rican Boys on 108th Street» (1955), «Andy Warhol» (1970), «Kate Millett» (1970, Time magazine cover), «Self-Portrait» (1980)
ficha.Now: Exhibition «Beautifully Imperfect», with around 90 works, at the Serralves Museum of Contemporary Art (Porto), until 17 January 2027 — the artist's first in Portugal

texto: Anyone visiting Serralves, in Porto, before 17 January has a rare opportunity: to see up close around 90 works by Alice Neel, one of the great American portraitists of the 20th century. The exhibition «Beautifully Imperfect», curated by Inês Grosso, is the painter's first in Portugal and, according to the museum, the largest ever held in Europe. It brings paintings lent by, among others, the National Portrait Gallery, in Washington, and the Whitney Museum, in New York.

Alice Neel was born in 1900, in Pennsylvania. When she told her mother she wanted to be an artist, she was told she was «only a girl». She did not give up: she studied at an art school for women in Philadelphia and married the Cuban painter Carlos Enríquez, with whom she lived in Havana. Her personal life was hard: she lost a baby daughter and her second daughter was taken far away by her husband. During the Great Depression she painted with the support of a public employment programme for artists and, from 1938, lived for more than 20 years in Spanish Harlem, New York's Latino neighbourhood, where she portrayed neighbours, friends and her sons.

Her style is unmistakable: strong outlines, often blue, direct colours and an unfiltered gaze. She painted people as she saw them — tired, pregnant, ageing, nervous. She called herself a «collector of souls». She did so at a time when American art was in thrall to abstract painting, and so recognition came late: her first major retrospective, at the Whitney, was in 1974, when she was already 74. At Serralves, the visit opens with her 1980 «Self-Portrait», in which she paints herself naked, aged 80, brush in hand.

A few curiosities. In 1970 she painted Andy Warhol seated, bare-chested, with the scars from the shooting he had survived two years earlier. That same year she made the portrait of the feminist writer Kate Millett for the cover of Time magazine, from a photograph, because Millett refused to sit. In the 1940s she bought back some of her own paintings, which had been sold by weight, at four cents a pound (about half a kilo). She appeared in the Beat Generation film «Pull My Daisy» (1959) and, in 1984, was a guest on Johnny Carson's talk show. She died that year, in New York, aged 84.

cultura.titulo: Did you know that the best-selling café chair of all time had only six wooden parts and travelled flat-packed, 36 at a time, in a one-cubic-metre crate?
texto: Did you know that you have very probably sat on a chair designed in 1859? It is called No. 14, is known as the «café chair» or «bistro chair» and was created by the German cabinetmaker Michael Thonet, in Vienna. It is made of bent beech wood, with a round cane seat and an arched back. By 1930 more than 50 million had been made. It is still manufactured today.

The secret is in the wood. In the 1830s, Thonet began bending wood instead of carving it. In 1855 he worked out how to do it with solid wood: he softened beech rods with steam and bent them in moulds, with a metal strip fixed to the outside so the wood would not crack. It was cheaper than gluing together several thin sheets, and his patents gave him a near-monopoly on the technique for years. The main factory was in Moravia, in today's Czech Republic, close to beech forests and the railway.

Then came the idea that changed the furniture trade. The No. 14 chair has just six wooden parts — two front legs, one piece forming the back legs and backrest, an inner arch, the seat and a foot ring — held together with ten screws and two nuts. So it could travel in pieces: one crate of one cubic metre held 36 chairs, which were assembled by shops or distributors at their destination. Transport became much cheaper, and the chair reached cafés all over the world. According to the Victoria and Albert Museum, in London, it was among the first pieces of furniture to be mass-produced and shipped knocked-down — a grandmother of the shelves we now buy in flat boxes.

It set an example. According to the Design Museum, in London, the architect Le Corbusier is said to have remarked that nothing more elegant and more practical had ever been created. In 1869 the patent expired and No. 14 became one of the most copied chairs in the world. In Vienna, cafés such as the Frauenhuber and the Tirolerhof still use it. And the current version, named 214, celebrated its 160th birthday in 2019.

cultura.titulo: Lisbon Photobook Fair: for 16 editions an informal group has brought photographers and small publishers together around the photobook

ficha.Origins: Created by an informal group (in 2015 it called itself «Os Novos Suspeitos», The New Suspects); supported by the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico (Lisbon's municipal photographic archive) since the 6th edition, in 2015
ficha.Participants: Photographers, self-publishing authors, independent publishers and booksellers and antiquarian booksellers specialising in photography
ficha.Field: Photography and publishing: photobooks (books in which the photographs tell the story) and «photozines»
ficha.Now: 16th edition from 27 to 29 November 2026, at the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico (Rua da Palma, 246); free entry

texto: A week from now, from Friday 27 to Sunday 29 November, the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico, Lisbon's municipal photographic archive on Rua da Palma, will fill up with photography books. It is the 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair (Feira do Livro de Fotografia de Lisboa), also called the Feira do Fotolivro, a yearly gathering of photographers, small publishers and specialist booksellers. Entry is free. It opens on Friday from 17:00 to 20:00 and at the weekend from 11:00 to 20:00.

First, what is a photobook? It is a book in which the photographs are not illustrations: they are what tells the story, through their order, their size and the dialogue between pages. Many are made in small print runs, by the authors themselves. The fair was born to give this world a space. Behind it is an informal group of people linked to photography — in 2015 it called itself «Os Novos Suspeitos» (The New Suspects) — which that year, at the 6th edition, gained the support of Lisbon City Council's photographic archive. The fair describes itself as an experimental space to show, sell and discuss photobooks, and to build new audiences.

How does it work? There is a market of new and rare books, with publishers and antiquarian booksellers; an exhibition of «dummies», the prototypes of books that do not yet exist, which visitors can leaf through and comment on; a space for self-publishing authors; and presentations of projects, finished or in progress. This year, Time Out Lisboa mentions, among others, Ghost Editions, XYZ Books, STET, Pierre von Kleist and the Alexandria bookshop. Past editions have had talks, workshops and even a guest country: Lithuania in 2014 and Brazil in 2015.

Why does it matter? Portugal has few bookshops devoted to photography, and many photobooks never reach ordinary bookshops. For more than a decade the fair has been a yearly meeting point for those who make and those who seek out these books, and a place where young photographers show work not yet published. It also leaves its mark on the archive itself: in 2015, most of the books from the Brazilian exhibition stayed afterwards in the Arquivo's library, where they can be consulted free of charge.

Russia attacked Ukraine overnight into Friday: three bridges in Kyiv damaged and at least five dead, according to provisional figures.
The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya: the first time it has found a state responsible for genocide.
Portugal's public sector is on a national strike today: according to the unions, rubbish collection stopped overnight in several municipalities and some schools may not open.
In the 2027 Budget, the PS and Chega approved zero VAT on a basket of foods from January to March, against the PSD, CDS-PP and IL.
COP31 reaches its scheduled last day with a draft deal that no longer mentions moving away from fossil fuels.
